role: Chat session capture and recovery across AI providers: workspace discovery, orphaned-session recovery, chronological merging, and full-text search over a harvested store. The one tool in the stack whose subject is the agent transcript itself, which is what makes an agent's own history durable rather than a side effect of whichever editor produced it.

capabilities.name: schema.ontology
capabilities.description: Emit the cross-provider ontology: entity types, relationships, and semantic tags.

capabilities.name: list
capabilities.description: List workspaces, sessions, or paths.

capabilities.name: find
capabilities.description: Search workspaces or sessions by text pattern across title, content, and id.

capabilities.name: show
capabilities.description: Show a workspace, session, or path.

capabilities.name: detect
capabilities.description: Auto-detect workspace and provider information.

capabilities.name: doctor
capabilities.description: Check system environment, providers, and configuration health.

capabilities.name: inspect
capabilities.description: Inspect editor state databases, session indices, caches, and file validity.

capabilities.name: fetch
capabilities.description: Fetch chat sessions from workspaces, sessions, or paths into the local store.

capabilities.name: harvest
capabilities.description: Harvest chat sessions from all providers into the unified database.

capabilities.name: sync
capabilities.description: Sync sessions between the harvest database and provider workspaces.

capabilities.name: import
capabilities.description: Import session files from external directories into a workspace.

capabilities.name: export
capabilities.description: Export chat sessions to files outside the store.

capabilities.name: merge
capabilities.description: Merge chat sessions from workspaces, sessions, or paths chronologically.

capabilities.name: move
capabilities.description: Move chat sessions between workspaces.

capabilities.name: shard
capabilities.description: Split oversized sessions into linked shards by request count or file size.

capabilities.name: recover
capabilities.description: Recover lost chat sessions from backups, recording state, or corrupted files.

capabilities.name: register
capabilities.description: Add on-disk sessions to the editor's database index, making orphaned sessions visible.

capabilities.name: migration
capabilities.description: Move chat sessions between machines.

capabilities.name: git
capabilities.description: Version chat sessions through git.

capabilities.name: provider
capabilities.description: Manage LLM provider configuration.

capabilities.name: telemetry
capabilities.description: Manage anonymous usage data collection.

capabilities.name: watch
capabilities.description: Watch agent session directories for changes and auto-harvest.

capabilities.name: api
capabilities.description: Start the HTTP API server that serves the web frontend.

capabilities.name: run
capabilities.description: Launch an AI coding agent with auto-save, or run interactive tools.

capabilities.name: agency
capabilities.description: Manage agents and orchestration through the agent development kit.

note: Declares the top-level command groups, not the 137 REST operations, which are routed and documented but not yet enumerated here; silence about them is not a claim that they are absent. Two capabilities draw a budget because they spend model tokens on repetition -- `run` launches an agent and `agency` orchestrates them. The rest are granted and unbudgeted because they move bytes already on this machine: repetition costs disk and time, not money, and marking them budgeted would make a budget mean two different things. Reversibility, consequence and scope are left undeclared rather than guessed; an unmeasured axis satisfies no requirement, which is the honest reading until someone establishes them.
